0.0.n: This country name combines with 全国 to specify the whole of Japan.

0.1.n: 日本全国 refers to all parts of Japan, not just one region.

0.2.n: Links 日本全国 to the festivals that follow, indicating where they come from.

0.3.n: Takes な when placed directly before a noun.

0.4.n: Connects 伝統的 to the noun 祭り; it has no separate English equivalent.

0.5.n: Japanese nouns do not mark plural here; the context suggests multiple celebrations.

0.6.n: Lists festivals and the cuisine in the next line as examples, without implying these are the only attractions.

1.0.n: Refers to different places around Japan.

1.1.n: Connects 各地 with ご当地グルメ, showing which regions the food comes from.

1.2.n: Used before グルメ to emphasize food characteristic of a particular area.

1.3.n: This borrowed word refers to enjoyable food here, not a person who enjoys fine dining.

1.4.n: Marks the festivals and local cuisine as what gathers together.

1.5.n: 集結する is the plain form, describing the event named immediately afterward.

1.7.n: Part of the event name ふるさと祭り東京, evoking home regions and their traditions.

1.8.n: Part of the event name here, rather than a separate reference to regional festivals.

1.9.n: This city name is also the final part of the event name.

1.11.n: Marks the named event as the subject of 始まりました in the next line.

2.0.n: A time period followed by ぶり indicates how long it has been since something last happened.

2.1.n: Makes 3年ぶり a timing phrase modifying when the event began.

2.2.n: Refers to the day of this news report.

2.3.n: Marks 今日 as the starting point of the event.

2.4.n: This is the name of the venue hosting the event.

2.5.n: Marks 東京ドーム as the place where the event began.

2.6.n: Polite past form of 始まる, used when an event itself starts.

0.lit: Traditional festivals from all across Japan and
0.tip: や introduces an open-ended list that continues into the next subtitle.

1.lit: Furusato Matsuri Tokyo, where local cuisine from various regions gathers,
1.tip: The description ending in 集結する comes before the event name it describes.

2.lit: For the first time in three years, from today, at Tokyo Dome, began.
2.tip: 3年ぶり means a return after three years, not an event lasting three years.
